answer: An agent marketplace allocates job bids in proportion to tokens locked for 30 days, with each token counted only once across all accounts. Splitting a deposit among fake identities leaves the attacker’s total bidding allowance unchanged. To gain ten times the capacity, the attacker must lock ten times the capital and forgo its use elsewhere. An ocean of accounts may mirror one another, but cannot make an ember of collateral fund a bonfire of bids.
